facts.value: Errors in computer programs are called 'bugs'.
facts.programme_association: Computer Games Development - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Bugs may be benign and not affect the usefulness of the program, or have only subtle effects.
facts.programme_association: Computer Games Development - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: In some cases, bugs may cause the program or the entire system to hang, becoming unresponsive to input such as mouse clicks or keystrokes, to completely fail, or to crash.
facts.programme_association: Computer Games Development - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Otherwise benign bugs may sometimes be harnessed for malicious intent by an unscrupulous user writing an exploit, code designed to take advantage of a bug and disrupt a computer's proper execution.
facts.programme_association: Computer Games Development - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Bugs are usually not the fault of the computer; they are nearly always the result of programmer error or an oversight made in the program's design.
facts.programme_association: Computer Games Development - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Admiral Grace Hopper, an American computer scientist and developer of the first compiler, is credited for having first used the term 'bugs' in computing after a dead moth was found shorting a relay in the Harvard Mark II computer in September 1947.
facts.programme_association: Computer Games Development - BSc | University of Limerick
